result.note: Tests the April 2026 RBI reporting mandate for offshore rupee derivatives: its scope and phasing, and the reporting body.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, the Reserve Bank of India ordered banks to report offshore rupee derivative trades executed by their group entities. Consider the following statements about this mandate:
items: Banks must report both deliverable and non-deliverable over-the-counter FX contracts.
Foreign lenders must disclose trades from their offshore units, not just their Indian branches.
Lenders must report 100% of notional value by July 2027.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: implementation is phased, with 70% of notional value due by July 2027 and 100% by July 2028. Trades under USD 1 million are exempt, and including offshore units closes a major loophole for foreign lenders.
questions.source: Lenders must report 70% of notional value by July 2027, hitting 100% by July 2028.

questions.prompt: Under the Reserve Bank of India's April 2026 mandate, banks must report offshore rupee derivative trades by their group entities to which of the following?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India
questions.explain: Banks must report deliverable and non-deliverable over-the-counter FX contracts to the Clearing Corporation of India. The move follows other RBI steps to manage the rupee, including a USD 100 million cap on net open positions.
questions.source: Banks must now report both deliverable and non-deliverable over-the-counter FX contracts to the Clearing Corporation of India.
